probe.text_sample: Your Page Title Ingrid Solberg © Work Courses Products Journal About Overview [email protected] Contact Menu Close 01 Work 02 Courses 03 Products 04 Journal 05 About 06 Overview 07 Contact [email protected] (Journal) Why the stoneware studio kept its old logo The client asked for a new logo. We ended up keeping the old one, and the identity is better for it. Written 12 September 2026 Reading 1 min read Topics identity process The brief said “new logo”. The first week of research said otherwise. Customers at the shop, the potters’ neighbours and even the local paper all described the studio by its little hand-drawn circle, the one on the kiln door since the garage days. Recognition is expensive A small business spends years earning the few seconds of recognition a mark gets on a shelf or a market stall. Throwing that away for something cleaner is a real cost, and it rarely shows up in a proposal. So instead of replacing the circle, we redrew it. Same idea, steadier line, a single weight that survives a rubber stamp and a debossing plate. Regulars noticed that something looked sharper. Nobody noticed that it had changed.
